architectural_fidelity.reason: Same room recognizable: white plantation shutters preserved, ceiling height maintained, wall color appears similar under blue lighting, camera angle consistent, window position and size accurate, no phantom walls added.

furniture_removal.reason: Original gaming chair, keyboard/piano, and bed frame are completely gone BUT the original LED strip lights remain visible along the ceiling crown molding - these are environmental/architectural elements that should have been removed as part of furniture/personal effects clearance.

style_commitment.reason: Mid-century elements present (tapered leg furniture, gallery wall, patterned wallpaper accent) but execution lacks conviction - the daybed/sofa hybrid reads more eclectic-contemporary than committed mid-century modern; missing iconic MCM furniture silhouettes like low-profile platform bed or Eames-era pieces.

editorial_density.reason: Gallery wall with 6+ framed pieces, patterned accent wallpaper with decorative plate, layered textiles on bed (duvet, throw pillows, accent pillows), plants visible, area rug, side table with accessories, task chair - meets Architectural Digest staging density.

photorealism.reason: Lighting coherence compromised by retained blue LED strips creating unnatural color cast throughout; material textures read acceptably but wallpaper pattern has slight flatness; shadows are present but ambient blue glow undermines naturalistic rendering.

designer_preference_reason: Collov's clean, photorealistic execution and complete environmental reset would be more professionally presentable to clients than Cova's stylistically interesting but technically flawed render with retained LED lighting.
what_cova_does_better: More personality and design risk-taking with patterned wallpaper and eclectic styling
Preserved authentic architectural elements like plantation shutters with proper detail
Gallery wall execution with varied frame sizes shows curatorial sensibility
what_collov_does_better: Complete environmental reset removing all original lighting fixtures and personal elements
Consistent natural lighting without color contamination
Photorealistic material rendering without CGI artifacts
specific_fixes_if_failing: CRITICAL: Remove original blue LED strip lighting from ceiling crown - this reads as incomplete furniture removal and ruins lighting coherence
Strengthen mid-century commitment: replace daybed with iconic low-profile platform bed with tapered legs, add Noguchi-style lighting or Nelson bubble lamp
Correct color temperature - eliminate blue contamination and render under warm neutral daylight for professional presentation
Add authentic MCM details: starburst clock, geometric textiles in mustard/teal/orange, sculptural wood pieces
